title: Security review: pen test results & patching cadence — Aurora Finance
summary: Redwood and Aurora Finance reviewed the recent pen test results and remediation progress, discussed vulnerability management and secure SDLC practices, and aligned on a patching cadence and next steps for outstanding findings. Action items include Redwood sending an annotated pen test report, Aurora sharing patching windows, and scheduling a follow-up in two weeks to review remediation status.
next_steps: Jordan to send annotated pen test report and remediation spreadsheet by 2026-03-30
Aurora to provide preferred maintenance windows and patching calendar by 2026-04-02
Schedule follow-up status call in two weeks (target 2026-04-11)
Priya to share runbook template for emergency patching and CVE triage
Maya to attach SOC 2 report and architecture diagram to CRM
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send annotated pen test PDF + remediation tracker - due 2026-03-30
Marisol Vega: Share Aurora patching maintenance windows and blackout dates - due 2026-04-02
Priya Kapoor: Provide emergency patching runbook and example scripts - due 2026-04-01
Ethan Park: Open tracking ticket for CVE-2026-0456 (app server) and assign to SRE - due 2026-03-31
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to walk through the pen test results and your remediation plan. Marisol, thanks for sending the report ahead of time.
[00:18] Marisol Vega: yeah thanks Jordan, quick note — the PDF had a couple of redacted things so i hope we can go over those, and there are a few priority items that came up in the web app layer.
[00:32] Priya Kapoor: hi all, i'm Priya from Redwood infra security, i'll start with the high-level findings and then we can dive into specifics. my notes — there were one critical, three high, and several medium/low items called out.
[00:48] Liam O'Connor: one critical? can you remind me what that was about, i skimmed and wasn't totally sure of the repro steps.
[01:02] Priya Kapoor: sure, it's the session fixation plus improper token invalidation on our legacy SSO integration path, the pen tester chained it with an open redirect to gain persistent access. we flagged it as critical because it allows long-lived session reuse if an attacker gets a token.
[01:24] Sofia Ramos: that's the old SAML bridge we've been planning to deprecate, we thought migrating to the new SSO provider would close it but sounds like the old path still exists in staging and slipped into prod routing.
[01:38] Jordan Lee: ok that maps to what you all sent. quick clarifying question — is that the reason you asked about session cookie rotation and KMS key rotation?
[01:50] Marisol Vega: yes, also we want to see how Redwood handles key management on your side — we need to demonstrate separation of keys for DB at rest vs token encryption per our SOC 2 checklist.
[02:04] Priya Kapoor: understood. on the Redwood side we use customer-scoped KMS keys for Private deployments and envelope encryption in Hosted; there's a key rotation cadence and options for HSM-backed keys. apologies if some of the product names in the report are fuzzy — the auto-transcript typed K-M-S as "kay-em-ess" in a few spots.
[02:24] Ethan Park: random question — do you provide an audit log for admin actions with immutable retention? compliance needs us to keep logs for seven years in some geos.
[02:38] Jordan Lee: yes, we have per-tenant audit logs; retention tiers are configurable. default retention for hosted is 90 days but enterprise customers can add longer retention with archive to your cloud bucket or to our long-term storage add-on. we can map to your EU residency rules and ship logs to your GCP bucket in eu-west1.
[02:58] [00:03:00] Marisol Vega: great — in the pen test there were two medium items marked as "configuration drift" on our dedicated instances that relate to outdated kernel packages. one is an App server kernel at 4.14 that the tester said has a known CVE.
[03:18] Priya Kapoor: do you run unified patching across dedicated pools or do you patch per-customer?
[03:26] Ethan Park: we currently patch per-cluster; we have weekly windows but historically some customers request staggered windows so we delay. the issue is automation — we've been behind on a couple of upstream kernel backports.
[03:40] Jordan Lee: ok let's capture that — Priya, can you walk Aurora through our suggested patching cadence and emergency patch flow?
[03:48] Priya Kapoor: absolutely. recommended cadence is monthly scheduled patching for non-critical updates, with weekly micro-updates for package managers if you want. for critical CVEs we recommend our 24-72 hour emergency patch workflow: triage, test in staging with canary, and rollback plan. We also maintain a CVE broadcast channel and a vulnerability tracker with severity tags.
[04:12] Marisol Vega: sounds reasonable. for demonstrability to auditors we need to show triage tickets and dates — can Redwood provide exported CSVs of vulnerability events and remediation timestamps?
[04:26] Jordan Lee: yes we can provide exported remediation timelines per ticket and we can attach them to the SOC 2 evidence folder. we'll also annotate the pen test report with remediation cutlines.
[04:38] [00:04:40] Liam O'Connor: can you also confirm whether Redwood runs SAST/DAST scans as part of your secure SDLC or is that customer responsibility?
[04:52] Priya Kapoor: Redwood has internal SAST for our platform code and we run regular third-party DAST on our public endpoints. for private deployments, we recommend customers integrate their SAST/SCA tools in CI; we provide a guidance doc and sample pipelines. i will share that doc after the call.
[05:10] Sofia Ramos: small nit — the pen test report references a "KV cache" issue, but the tester spelled it "K V cash" in places which made it hard to follow. it's actually a serialized cache key issue we fixed in december, is that in scope of today's review?
[05:26] Priya Kapoor: thank you, yes that was a transcription/typo issue in the report, the underlying issue was an inconsistent cache key handling in older model-serving code; devs patched it and we verified with the tester. we'll mark that as remediated in the tracker.
[05:40] [00:06:00] Marisol Vega: moving to encryption — auditors want to see key rotation policies and proof of encryption in transit and at rest. specifically, can you show us KMS key rotation logs and your HSM usage for Private deployment?
[05:56] Jordan Lee: we'll provide KMS rotation logs and HSM attestations where applicable. for Hosted we use envelope encryption and rotate at least quarterly by default; for Private you can bring your own KMS or we can integrate with your HSM.
[06:10] Ethan Park: how about backups? are DB backups encrypted with separate keys?
[06:17] Priya Kapoor: yes, backups are encrypted with a separate customer-scoped key and we support key rotation for backups as well. we'll include the backup key policy in the artifact pack.
[06:30] [00:06:45] Marisol Vega: there was also a request in the report about RBAC — testers found a service account with overly broad permissions. we closed the immediate exposure but we'd like Redwood's assistance auditing cross-tenant roles for our Dedicated instance.
[06:48] Jordan Lee: we can run a role audit and provide a report of principals and effective permissions. Priya, is there anything special we need from Aurora to run that?
[06:58] Priya Kapoor: yes we'll need a list of service accounts, and if you have any custom roles please share the role definition. we can run an IAM analysis tool and produce a CSV of role bindings and recommended least-privilege changes.
[07:10] Liam O'Connor: timeline?
[07:14] Priya Kapoor: we can turn that around in three to five business days after we get the role list.
[07:20] [00:07:20] Sofia Ramos: one other finding — the pen tester noted missing immutable logs for a subset of admin console actions; they could delete entries in staging. does Redwood provide WORM-style logging or append-only archives?
[07:34] Jordan Lee: we have append-only audit streams; for longer-term immutability we can export to your object store with immutable bucket settings, or provide an append-only archive with signed manifests. we'll include options in the doc.
[07:46] Marisol Vega: perfect. next, vulnerability management — how do you categorize severity? is it pure CVSS or do you use compensating factors like exposure and exploit maturity?
[08:00] Priya Kapoor: we start with CVSS but then apply environmental factors: whether a vulnerable service is internet-facing, exploit maturity, whether it's mitigated by network policies, and business impact. our tracker allows you to override severity based on your environment.
[08:18] [00:08:18] Ethan Park: regarding timelines, the pen test shows a kernel CVE that we can't live with in prod. what's Redwood's recommended approach for dedicated pools — can you pin a pool and do emergency rolling kernel updates without downtime?
[08:32] Jordan Lee: yes we recommend pinned pools for critical workloads; our dedicated offering supports live migration and rolling upgrades with drain + canary to avoid full downtime. there is a short interruption for kernel-level patches in some stacks; we'll share specifics for your OS.
[08:48] Priya Kapoor: also note that for some older kernels we recommend in-place reprovisioning to a newer image rather than patching if backports are unsupported. we'll document recommended images and migration steps.
[09:00] [00:09:00] Marisol Vega: auditors will also ask for change control evidence. can Redwood provide a changelog for platform updates that affected Aurora's Dedicated pool?
[09:12] Jordan Lee: yes we can provide per-tenant change logs and release notes for any platform changes that were applied to your pool. those can be stamped with date/time and linked to the remediation tickets.
[09:22] Liam O'Connor: a bit of pushback from our infra team — they want reassurances that patching won't break model-serving latency SLAs during business hours. any suggestions for scheduling?
[09:36] Priya Kapoor: we typically recommend scheduling kernel and heavy infra patches during your low-traffic windows; for model-serving we suggest canaries on a fraction of traffic and metric-based rollback thresholds. if you want we can run a small synthetic benchmark during patch canary to validate latency.
[09:56] [00:10:00] Sofia Ramos: quick question — in the pen test remediation tracker, there's an outstanding medium item labeled "dependency SCA alert" for a third-party JS library. it's marked as low risk but the tester recommended upgrade. is there a reason we might delay that?
[10:12] Ethan Park: often we delay due to dependency compatibility and test run times in CI, but that shouldn't be an excuse — we'll prioritize.
[10:20] Jordan Lee: ok flag that as actionable — Priya, can you share our SCA guidance and an example PR template for dependency upgrades?
[10:28] Priya Kapoor: yes will do. we'll include an example CI job and a suggested rollback process if a dependency upgrade causes regressions.
[10:36] [00:10:40] Marisol Vega: the last bit from auditors — evidence for SOC 2: access reviews, MFA enforcement, and vendor risk assessments. we need a package that includes your SOC 2 letter and a vendor questionnaire answer.
[10:50] Jordan Lee: Maya can attach our SOC 2 report and a completed vendor risk questionnaire. Maya, can you confirm?
[10:56] Maya Chen: yes i'll upload both to CRM after the call and share a link.
[11:02] [00:11:02] Liam O'Connor: great. lets recap outstanding critical items and owners. the session fixation critical — who is leading?
[11:10] Priya Kapoor: Aurora devs need to remove legacy SAML bridge from prod routing; we can help with a mitigation pattern — immediate mitigation is adding strict token invalidation on logout and rotating session secret, full remediation is removing the legacy path or putting a firewall rule.
[11:28] Sofia Ramos: noted, i'll create a ticket for the SAML bridge removal and work with Ethan to schedule a deploy.
[11:36] Ethan Park: will do, estimated ETA 72 hours for mitigation and two weeks for full removal pending testing.
[11:44] [00:11:44] Marisol Vega: for reporting to auditors we'll need dates on the mitigation and the final removal.
[11:50] Jordan Lee: noted — please include those dates in the ticket and we'll pull them into the remediation tracker.
[11:58] Priya Kapoor: one more technical note — the pen tester exploited an open redirect that lived in an old marketing endpoint; recommend adding an allow-list on redirects and using relative paths. small change but high impact.
[12:12] [00:12:12] Sofia Ramos: thank you, we'll prioritize that as well.
[12:18] Jordan Lee: ok i think we're near the end of the hour. quick check — any blockers on Redwood's side for providing artifacts?
[12:26] Maya Chen: i'll gather the SOC2, KMS rotation logs, and the annotated pen test. expect those by Monday EOD.
[12:34] Marisol Vega: that's perfect. also we'd like the remediation tracker exported as CSV for auditor review.
[12:40] Jordan Lee: we'll do that.
[12:44] [00:12:44] Liam O'Connor: final ask from our side — can Redwood provide an example of your secure SDLC checklist that we can adapt?
[12:54] Priya Kapoor: yes, we'll include SAST/DAST cadence, code review requirements, dependency SCA, secrets scanning, and release gating steps.
[13:06] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with artifacts and tee up the April 11th status call. if anything urgent pops up we'll use the vulnerability channel.
[13:16] Marisol Vega: thanks all.
[13:20] [END]
